title: Curvature-Guided Task Synergy for Skeleton based Temporal Action Segmentation
claim: Prior pipelines share features across decoupled task heads and lose cross-task synergy; ours couples tasks through geometric curvature signals.
layout: 4 panels: two pipeline panels left, two inset concept panels right, dashed dividers
description: Four panels separated by dashed lines. Panel (a) shows the existing approach, a bottom-up stack: skeleton sequences (blue box), a green spatio-temporal encoder, and shared features feeding separate Cls. Head (orange) and Loc. Head (red) via arrows. Red text and a dashed red cross mark 'Information Silos / Missing Cross-task Synergy'. Panel (b) has the same encoder and skeleton input, but it splits into Cls. Experts (yellow) and Loc. Experts (pink). These feed the heads, with a bidirectional arrow between them and a circular 'Curvature-based Synergy' loop. Panel (c) top right shows a representation space: a blue cluster with a zigzag trajectory (high curvature) and a yellow cluster (low curvature), joined by a red transition path. Panel (d) shows the Cls and Loc heads linked to curvature and boundary sequence plots through bidirectional arrows. The eye goes first to the red warning text in (a), then to the loop in (b).
caption: (a) Existing STAS approaches. (b) The proposed method. (c) Classification representations create compact clusters, forcing high trajectory curvature within action segments. (d) Curvature-guided task collaboration.
abstract: Fine-grained temporal action segmentation plays a vital role in comprehensivehuman behavior understanding, with skeleton-based approaches (STAS) gaining prominence for their privacy and robustness. A core challenge in STAS arises from the conflicting feature requirements of action classification (demanding temporal invariance) and boundary localization (requiring temporal sensitivity). Existing methods typically adopt decoupled pipelines, unfortunately overlooking the inherent semantic complementarity between these sub-tasks, leading to information silos that prevent beneficial cross-task synergies. To address this challenge, we propose CurvSeg, a novel approach that synergizes classification and localization within the STAS domain through a unique geometric curvature guidance mechanism. Our key innovation lies in exploiting curvature properties of well-learned classification representations on skeleton sequences. Specifically, we observe that high curvature within action segments and low curvature at transitions effectively serve as geometric priors for precise boundary detection. CurvSeg establishes a virtuous cycle: localization predictions, guided by these curvature signals, in turn dynamically refine the classification feature space to organize into a geometry conducive to clearer boundaries. To compute stable curvature signals from potentially noisy skeleton features, we further develop a dual-expert weighting mechanism within a Mixture of Experts framework, providing task-adaptive feature extraction. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CurvSeg signif-icantly enhances STAS performance across multiple benchmark datasets, achieving superior results and validating the power of geometric-guided task collaboration for this specific problem.
